correctness.rationale: PASS: The source RESULT.md explicitly defines the affine-normalized d-dimensional circular frustum, positive radii, center/axis normalization and both endpoint regimes. For an axis-aligned ellipsoid, conical-side containment is the support-function inequality As*m+sqrt(q+A^2 s^2 p)<=A, plus the two end-plane bounds. Direct substitution gives equality at the lateral side in both regimes; the end constraints and positive transverse radius hold, including s=0 and s=1/d. In the first regime the normalized latitude at s plus the upper/lower poles have weights w=(d-1)/(d(1-s^2)) and w_±=(1-w∓ws)/2; these are nonnegative precisely for s<=1/d and have mean zero and covariance I_d/d. In the second regime the touching latitude is 1/d and weights are d/(d+1) for the latitude and 1/(d+1) for the lower pole; their first and second moments again satisfy John's criterion. Rotational averaging (not an assumption of optimality) supplies valid contact measures, so the global John theorem gives maximal volume and uniqueness among all ellipsoids. Independent symbolic equations and 95 numerical regimes were checked with the saved independent_checks.py; those samples do not prove the all-d statement.

final_claim: For every d>=2 and R>=r>0, the unique John ellipsoid of the right circular frustum has m=0,p=1,q=Rr if s=(R-r)/(R+r)<=1/d, and m=(1-ds)/(s(d+1)), p=(1+m)^2, q=(d-1)R^2/(d+1) otherwise. The cap-contact transition is r/R=(d-1)/(d+1).
limitations: Only positive smaller end radii, right circular frusta, and affine height changes; not arbitrary oblique frusta.
